chunks: Say: "We believe in God, and in what has been revealed to us, and in what had been sent down to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and their offspring, and what had been revealed to Moses and to Jesus and to all other prophets by their Lord. We make no distinction between them, and we submit to Him and obey."
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about belief in all prophets?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the principle of *Tawhid al-Anbiya* (Unity of the Prophets), affirming that all prophets preached the same core monotheistic message, thereby validating the continuity of divine revelation. It serves as a theological basis for respecting previous scriptures while recognizing the finality of Prophet Muhammad's message, emphasizing that true submission (*Islam*) is consistent across all eras. This perspective reinforces the Shia view of the *Ahl al-Bayt* as the rightful inheritors and interpreters of this unified prophetic tradition.
